All code should have single, well-defined responsibilities. Avoid duplicating logic and functionality across multiple files. Refactor repetitive code blocks into reusable components; document reusable components clearly. Strive for simplicity in design and implementation. Minimize complexity wherever possible. Avoid over-engineering solutions. Prioritize readability and understandability.

Follow SOLID principles: single responsibility; extend through new classes/modules rather than modifying existing ones; preserve correctness under substitution; depend only on used interfaces; high-level modules depend on abstractions, not low-level modules.

Only implement functionality that is currently required. Don't introduce features or code that is not explicitly needed. Focus on delivering working code, not anticipating future requirements.

Use consistent formatting/style (2-space indentation), meaningful names, and comments for complex logic. Each file should be cohesive; separate concerns into distinct modules/components with descriptive filenames. Include a README with an overview and instructions. Add docstrings to all functions, classes, and modules. Code length should be limited to 180 lines; each function or class should ideally be under 60 lines. Avoid unnecessary statements or blank lines. Inline comments should be used judiciously and explain complex logic.

Minimum: 80% code coverage. Test critical functionality, using unit tests for components and integration tests for interactions. Write testable code; refactor regularly. Prioritize maintainability, collaborate, and review/improve c
